limits: User confirmed immediate low-stock and overdue-invoice delivery. Fresh unique QA adjustment/invoice references and new notification IDs provide causal checks; the duplicate-alert policy is unspecified and not guessed.

Header bell count/panel, actual new low/out-of-stock alerts, owned alert read persistence, live header count refresh before reload, linked product navigation and type/priority queries are exercised. Read-back uses the main paginated All feed, not the separate high-priority counter query.

Overdue testing creates a new invoice already due yesterday, then changes it from Draft to Pending with Rs100 unpaid. Natural calendar crossing on an existing invoice and scheduler internals are not certified.

Preferences are temporarily isolated to in-app delivery with email/push/SMS and quiet hours disabled, then exactly restored. Any legacy email boolean settings are also disabled during the test and restored. No browser push permission is enabled.

Only current-test alerts are marked read; existing alerts are not deleted or globally marked. Owned invoices are cancelled before original preferences are restored; all five QA stock balances are restored. Synthetic cancelled invoices and adjustment history remain.
automation: Initial focused notification-center run passed before broader invoice/stock scenarios.

Corrected a response-selection race: the header/main page makes several GETs to the same notification endpoint. Feed reads now require the actual main All query (20 per page, page1, no type/severity/unread-only filter). Read persistence can paginate to the owned alert.
Added a fresh unread-count response and matching header badge assertion after marking the owned alert read, before any navigation/reload. This passes in the corrected run.

Invoice correlation accepts the actual invoice reference or invoice action URL. An uncorrelated new overdue alert is a blocker, not a falsely confirmed missing-alert bug. No exact notification wording/duplicate policy is assumed.
Public fingerprinted assets use the shared unchanged-byte cache; all notification/business APIs stay live. Earlier automation errors are superseded by focused/full reruns.

bugs.title: Issuing an already overdue unpaid invoice produces no immediate in-app alert
steps: Sign in to Nexstock QA Company and open Notifications > Settings.
Enable In-App and Invoice Due Reminders; disable quiet hours for the check. Use in-app delivery only.

Ensure the disposable QA inventory product has sufficient stock. Create an invoice for QA Billing Automation Customer with one QA item priced Rs100, issue date 10 October 2026 and due date 24 October 2026 (test date 25 October).
Save as Draft, then use Change Status to set Pending. Confirm the invoice remains unpaid with Rs100 outstanding and the past due date.
Immediately open Notifications and inspect fresh All/overdue alerts for the new invoice, allowing 30 seconds for delivery.
bugs.expected: Once the invoice is eligible and unpaid past its due date, an immediate in-app overdue alert identifies that invoice, consistent with the user's confirmed timing contract.
bugs.actual: The independent and integrated scenarios create valid past-due unpaid invoices, but no new matching overdue/invoice-due alert appears during the bounded observation window. Fresh main-feed reads contain no ambiguous new invoice alert either. One reproduced full-flow reference is INV-0Z2K2J.
bugs.comment: Evaluate overdue alert eligibility when the invoice becomes an unpaid past-due record, and deliver it immediately while respecting company scope, preferences and deduplication. The UI evidence does not establish whether an event, worker or scheduler is the root cause. Test invoices are cancelled during cleanup; create a new QA invoice for manual reproduction. Natural due-date crossing should also be tested after the fix.
